Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L07 GP Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Scenario: A student is preparing a presentation about source evaluation. Which choice best shows a clear perspective and coherent focus? \

answer.text: A. The presentation lists several unrelated school topics.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: B. The presentation uses a decorative image with no explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: C. The presentation avoids stating what the audience should understand.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: D. The presentation states one clear point about source evaluation and uses details that support that point.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L07 GP Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Slide note: A student wants to support a presentation about revision clarity. Which slide note is most audience-ready? \

answer.text: A. Lots of stuff about revision clarity and other things.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: B. Concise evidence connects revision clarity to the presentation perspective.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

answer.text: C. A copied paragraph with every source detail on one slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: D. An unrelated sentence that does not support the message.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

Question ID: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 U06 L07 GP Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03 Speaker note: A slide gives a short point about peer feedback. Which speaker note best explains rather than repeats the slide? \

answer.text: A. This point matters because it helps the audience understand how peer feedback supports the overall message.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

answer.text: B. I will read the slide exactly as written.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: C. This slide is here because it is on the screen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: D. Now I will talk about a different topic.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

Question ID: MLA.ENG1.W.04 U06 L07 GP Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 Revision task: Which change would most improve clarity for a presentation about \

answer.text: A. Replace vague wording with precise language that names the communication purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

answer.text: B. Add more unrelated facts to make the slide longer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: C. Remove the perspective so the audience can guess the point.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: D. Use smaller text so a paragraph fits on the slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.03 U06 L07 GP Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.W.03 Readiness check: Which final check best prepares a presentation about research evidence for an audience? \

answer.text: A. Check only whether the slides have colors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: B. Add new unrelated content at the end.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: C. Confirm that slides, speaker notes, evidence, and wording support the same audience-focused message.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

answer.text: D. Ignore conventions and source reliability.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.
